name: vi-history-suite
description: VS Code extension for content-detected LabVIEW VI history review in Git repositories.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: VI History disables selected-file history evaluation and comparison execution in untrusted workspaces to prevent external process execution. Documentation and local runtime settings CLI preparation remain available.

viHistorySuite.strictRsrcHeader.description: Use stricter checks when deciding whether a file is a real LabVIEW VI. Leave this off unless files are being wrongly accepted or rejected.

viHistorySuite.historyWindowMode.description: How many past versions to load. Auto shows the full history when it is a manageable size; capped limits it to the number set in Max History Entries.

viHistorySuite.maxHistoryEntries.description: The most past versions to show when History Window Mode is set to capped.

viHistorySuite.runtimeProvider.description: Where comparisons run: Host uses the LabVIEW installed on your machine (default); Docker uses an NI LabVIEW container image. Most people leave this on Host.

viHistorySuite.labviewVersion.description: Which LabVIEW year to use for comparisons (for example 2025 or 2026). LabVIEW 2025 and newer can open older VIs without converting them first.

viHistorySuite.labviewBitness.description: Whether to use 32-bit (x86) or 64-bit (x64) LabVIEW for comparisons. Match this to the LabVIEW you have installed.

viHistorySuite.labviewExePath.description: Optional: the full path to your LabVIEW program (LabVIEW.exe on Windows, labview on Linux). Set this only if VI History cannot find LabVIEW automatically.

viHistorySuite.labviewCliPath.description: Optional: the full path to the LabVIEW CLI (LabVIEWCLI). Set this only if VI History cannot find it automatically; this also lets VI History open when the LabVIEW CLI cannot be detected.

viHistorySuite.container.imageVersion.description: Which LabVIEW Docker image to use for Docker comparisons (for example 2026q1-windows). Leave empty to use the newest supported image. Run the VI History: Runtime & Report Settings command to pick from images available on Docker Hub or already downloaded; new National Instruments patches and years appear automatically.

viHistorySuite.preview.enabled.description: Turn on VI Preview (Docker runtime only): opening a LabVIEW VI (.vi/.vit/.vim/.ctl) renders it as a read-only picture of its front panel and block diagram, and the extension silently caches every VI in the repository in the background. Off by default. Manage this from the VI History: Runtime & Report Settings command — the toggle appears there when Docker is selected.

enumDescriptions: Only pre-render in the background when comparisons run in Docker, so your installed LabVIEW is never tied up. Recommended default.
Also pre-render in the background when using your installed (Host) LabVIEW, so you see caching progress on Host too. This keeps LabVIEW busy while it caches a large workspace.
Never pre-render previews in the background.
viHistorySuite.preview.backgroundWarming.description: After you open a VI preview, whether VI History quietly pre-renders the other VIs in the workspace so they open instantly, shown as a caching percentage in the status bar. Docker-only (default) skips this when using Host so your LabVIEW stays free; choose Always to see caching progress on Host too.

viHistorySuite.runtime.cliConnectTimeout.description: How long (in seconds) to wait for LabVIEW to start before a comparison gives up. Increase this if the first comparison after opening VS Code times out on a slow machine. Default is 180.

viHistorySuite.report.ignoreViAttributes.description: Leave VI attribute changes out of the comparison report.

viHistorySuite.report.ignoreFrontPanel.description: Leave all front-panel changes out of the comparison report.

viHistorySuite.report.ignoreFrontPanelOb.description: Leave front-panel changes that are only moves or resizes out of the comparison report.

viHistorySuite.report.ignoreBlockDiagram.description: Leave all block-diagram changes out of the comparison report.
Ignore cosmetic block-diagram changes (such as moving or resizing items) so the report shows only changes that affect behavior.

scripts.test:integration: npm run compile && npm run test:integration:compile && node out-tests/tests/integration/runTests.js
scripts.package: npm run compile && npm run package:audit && node scripts/runPinnedVsce.js package
